answer: A lagoon authority buys forecasts of erosion on its basalt shore. Agents run a numerical kernel on fresh sensor batches; each paid slot requires a signed, single-use compute lease and a random simultaneous benchmark. The scheduler accepts one result per lease, so fifty fake names sharing one GPU cannot multiply slots or reuse work. To collect fifty payouts, an attacker must rent parallel compute, obtain distinct leases and meet deadlines. A provider could sell bogus leases or collude on benchmarks, so audit provider logs and compare outputs with independent stations.
